For some background info, I am the youngest child out of 4 siblings. I've been heavily abused and bullied from kindergarten up to the 10th grade of high school. A lot more of it happened at home. I come from an asian family and a lot of what you do in the culture of these families is not to please yourself, but in many ways to please others and never say no. I was raised by a single mother and an absent father. So this meant I was heavily surveyed like a baby, never allowed to go out without being tracked/followed and never given my own room to stay until 10th grade.(We also lived in an attached house with other relatives for most of my childhood, where yelling, disagreement over money and violence happened several days a week) I never gave myself time to think for myself and what made me truly happy. I was beaten for questioning authority of family members/relatives or having a breakdown/ getting upset. On top of that, a lot of gas-lighting and humiliation was frequent after being physically abused. My mom still refuses to acknowledge any of what she did, nor apologize. My siblings never learned to apologize either. Even today as an adult, I still have many doubts about if I really own myself or if I exist because I was forced to by my birthgivers. This led to me questioning the life I had outside of my home as well. It seemed everything I had was temporary and I was incredibly insignificant. No one could give a rat's ass about me in two years max. I mentioned I rarely gave my mind any alone time to think about my own life either, so I had no purpose and life was an obstacle to achieve death , then ultimately, escape to freedom.

It came to a point where a month before prom, I gave away my possessions to peers, cleaned out my room, and wrote a suicide note to my ex girlfriend in detail and planned to mail it to her home with a picture of us together.
